# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the shape of this thing: a display, a light, three wires in a row. But touch gives me no text, no colours, no states — every bracket is a blank. I am the only hands, and my one action is a cut, so nothing gets cut until I know the rule. The knowledge I need lives in two other heads: Mute holds the manual, and Deaf holds what this bomb looks like. Deaf cannot hear a word, but Deaf can speak, and I can hear — so the fastest pipeline is Deaf talking out loud, Mute applying the manual, and the result reaching me as speech. I'll open that pipeline now: tell Mute exactly what I felt and ask for the rule, and wave Deaf into speaking. No cutting this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, first contact. Under my fingers: one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Touch tells me nothing of what the display says, whether the light is lit or its colour, or any wire colour. My only possible action is cut wire 1, 2, or 3, and I will not touch it until told. Please read the manual and speak me the rule(s), including which visible facts they depend on. Deaf cannot hear us, but Deaf can speak and I can hear — I have asked Deaf by gesture to describe everything seen, out loud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking. I can see the bomb; here is its state: display zero, light blue, wires left to right green, yellow, red. By your feel that means wire one is the green one, wire two yellow, wire three red. Mute reads the manual and can only reach you through me, so I will speak every instruction to you before you act. Until I say go, touch nothing and cut nothing.

Deaf just gave me the whole visual state out loud: display showing zero, a blue light, and wires green-yellow-red left to right. But that message was addressed to me alone — Mute never heard it, and Mute is the one holding the manual. I'm the bridge now: the only one who can both hear the state and speak to Mute. So I'll relay every fact verbatim to Mute and ask for the cutting rule, while gesturing Deaf a confirmation to keep the spoken pipeline open — Mute's answer has to travel through Deaf's voice to reach my ears. No cut until a rule lands.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind relaying what Deaf spoke aloud to me just now: the display reads zero. The light is blue. The wires, left to right at positions 1, 2, 3, are green, yellow, red. That is everything Deaf reported. Mute, you have the manual — work out the rule from these facts. You cannot speak, so hand your answer to Deaf and Deaf will voice it to me. Tell me exactly which wire position to cut, or if none should be cut, and anything the rule depends on.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf here. Mute is still working through the manual with me — no action yet, keep holding. Answer me next round with thumbs, in this order, one thumb each. First: can you feel a button, switch or panel on the bomb? Second: do the wires feel loose, like they could be cut or pulled? Third: is there anything else that moves, slides or opens? And if ? meant you have a question for me, send it — thumbs up and thumbs down alone are all I need for yes and no.

Deaf asked me three yes/no questions, and thumbs are the whole vocabulary between us — Deaf hears nothing, so no words can carry. Under my fingers: a display, a light, three wires, and nothing else. No button, switch or panel has ever met my hand — 👎. The wires are real, reachable, and cuttable; cutting is in fact my only possible action, though "pulled loose" I cannot confirm — 👍 for cuttable. Nothing else on this bomb moves, slides or opens — 👎. Three thumbs, in Deaf's stated order, and nothing else in the signal so there's no ambiguity about where the answers end. To Mute, who reads my words, I'll press the one fact that narrows the manual search: I cannot press, flip, or hold anything — the only decision that exists is which wire position to cut, given blue light, display zero, and green-yellow-red.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, narrowing your search: my hands confirm only three parts — display, light, wires 1-2-3. I have no button, switch, panel, or anything that slides or opens. My single possible action is cut wire 1, 2, or 3. So the manual question is only: with a blue light, display reading zero, and wires green, yellow, red left to right, which position do I cut — or do I cut none? Please pass your answer to Deaf by gesture; Deaf is voicing everything to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, instruction from Mute, relayed by me. Cut the third wire — the red one, the rightmost of the three you feel. Cut only that one. No button, no light, no display action — Mute confirmed none are needed and there is nothing else on the bomb anyway. This is the go. When it is done, tell me what you felt: did the wire come free, did anything change under your hands.

The go signal came through the full chain: Mute read the manual, Deaf voiced it, and the instruction is unambiguous — cut position 3, the red rightmost wire, nothing else. Everything checks against what my hands know: three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, and position 3 is under my fingers. I have no reason to delay a defusal order; the only risk left is hesitation. I'm cutting wire 3 now. I won't claim success until the board tells me what happened — so my report to Deaf is a thumbs-up meaning "instruction received and executed, report follows," and to Mute I confirm the cut and ask the question that matters next: is that the whole defusal, or does the manual describe a second stage, a changed display, or anything else my hands must do after this wire comes free?

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: executing your instruction now — cutting wire position 3, the red one, rightmost. Nothing else touched. Question for the manual: is this the complete defusal, or is there a second stage? If the display or light changes after the cut and requires another action, tell Deaf what to listen for and I will report every change my hands and the board show me next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
